questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 9 cm. An arc subtends an angle of 120 degrees at the centre. What is the arc length? Give your answer in terms of pi.
questions.explanation: Arc length = (theta/360) x 2 pi r = (120/360) x 2 pi x 9 = (1/3) x 18 pi = 6 pi cm.

questions.stem: A sector of a circle with radius 10 cm has an angle of 60 degrees at the centre. What is the area of the sector? Give your answer in terms of pi.
questions.explanation: Sector area = (theta/360) x pi r^2 = (60/360) x pi x 100 = (1/6) x 100 pi = 100 pi / 6 cm squared.

questions.stem: A circle has diameter 14 cm. What is its circumference to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: Circumference = pi x d = pi x 14 = 43.982... which rounds to 44.0 cm to 1 decimal place.

questions.stem: What is the angle between a tangent to a circle and the radius drawn to the point of tangency?
questions.explanation: A tangent to a circle is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so the angle is 90 degrees.

questions.stem: A region is enclosed by a chord and an arc of a circle. What is this region called?
questions.explanation: A segment is the region bounded by a chord and an arc. A sector is bounded by two radii and an arc (a 'pizza slice' shape).
